newsitem.title: UK: Crime falls in Britain for 4th consecutive year.
newsitem.headline: Crime falls in Britain for 4th consecutive year.

text.p: The number of crimes committed in Britain fell for the fourth consecutive year in 1996 but violent crime rose by 11 percent, according to figures released on Monday.

Home Secretary (interior minister) Michael Howard said the 1.3 percent overall drop in crimes recorded by the police showed the tide was turning and underlined the ruling Conservative Party's reputation for being tough on crime.
"People recognise that we are making an impact on crime, that we are turning the tide," Howard added.
He acknowledged that the crime figures were still too high and said he was particularly concerned about the rise in violent crime.

The statistics also showed that the amount of recorded crime had almost doubled since the Conservatives came to power in 1979 -- a fact seized on by the opposition Labour Party who said the Conservatives were failing to match their claim to be the party of law and order.

The annual figures were released only hours before Prime Minister John Major, whose party trails Labour by more than 20 points in opinion polls, was expected to announce a May 1 date for a national election.
